title: Spooky stories behind two Birmingham pubs among the most haunted in the UK
excerpt: Birmingham pubs have been named among the UK's most haunted watering holes.
content:
With Halloween approaching, pub and restaurant discovery website Eat Drink Meet has listed 13 venues across the country said to have paranormal pasts.

Birmingham appears twice, with The Fighting Cocks in Moseley and The Trocadero on Temple Street included in the list.

The Fighting Cocks is said to be haunted by a former landlord who met a tragic end in the cellar.

The Fighting Cocks, Saint Mary's Row, Moseley, Birmingham. (Image: GSV)

According to information released by Eat Drink Meet, staff have reported unusual events since his death.

Glasses have apparently flown from shelves, while unexplained cold spots have also been experienced inside the pub.

Despite the claims, the Moseley venue remains a popular drinking spot, described as loved by locals for its friendly and laid-back atmosphere.

Visitors making a Halloween trip can also find drinks behind the bar, although the pub's alleged resident is said to be of a supernatural kind.

The Trocadero has a different history and an even longer list of reported incidents.

The Trocadero, Temple Street, Birmingham. (Image: Albert Chambers / Flickr)

The Grade II-listed building began as a fire engine house for the Norwich Union Insurance Company.

It became the Bodega wine bar in 1883, before being owned by Henry Skinner.

Skinner was murdered after a row over wages, according to the release.

Legend says he never completely left the building.

His ghost is claimed to knock over glasses, throw beer mats and fling loose change at customers and members of staff.

Two girls are also said to have fallen from a staircase inside the building.

Rumours say their ghosts haunt the pub as well.

Some staff are reportedly unconvinced, joking that the only spirits they have met are those served to customers.

Eat Drink Meet's remaining venues are The Mitre Bar in Edinburgh, The Hawes Inn in Queensferry, The Old White Swan and The Punch Bowl in York.

The list also includes The Spaniards Inn, The Volunteer and Williamson's Tavern in London.

Other entries are Fairfield Arms in Audenshaw, Toby Carvery Bolton, The Captain's Wife in Penarth and The Castle in the Peak District.

The claims include flying glasses, cold spots and former occupants who are said to remain at venues after death.

Eat Drink Meet published the list ahead of Halloween.
